s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly enlarging mass behind the ear with parietal bone invasion and vascular supply
salient_findings: Hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion on noncontrast CT
Heterogeneously enhancing lesion on Gadolinium-enhanced MRI
Vascular tumor supplied by the middle meningeal artery
key_facts: 76-year-old woman
History of appendicitis, torsion of an ovarian cyst pedicle, and uterine myoma
Mass enlarged over one month
No neurological deficits or systemic symptoms
Normal or negative laboratory studies, including complete blood counts, metabolic panel, and viral serology for HIV and Epstein-Barr virus
Noncontrast CT showed a 5-cm hyperdense meningeal mass
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed a heterogeneously enhancing lesion
Cerebral angiography demonstrated a vascular tumor supplied by the middle meningeal artery
Tumor was extradural and caused skull destruction with no intradural involvement

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical diagnosis and histology consistent with meningioma

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular tumor with extradural involvement and skull destruction

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to meningioma and possible extradural involvement

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant spindle cell neoplasm with positive immunostaining for α-smooth muscle actin

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Included in the differential diagnosis and possible consideration for malignant tumor

raw.rationale: The tumor's extradural location, vascular nature as demonstrated by cerebral angiography, and histological features of a malignant spindle cell neoplasm with positive immunostaining for α-smooth muscle actin, vimentin, and desmin are more consistent with hemangiopericytoma, a rare vascular tumor that can present with these characteristics.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Although initially considered due to the meningeal location, the histological and immunohistochemical findings do not support this diagnosis, as meningiomas typically have different immunostaining profiles and are less likely to be malignant spindle cell neoplasms.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: While solitary fibrous tumors can be vascular and have a similar location, the malignant features and specific immunohistochemical staining pattern in this case are less typical for solitary fibrous tumors, which are generally benign.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Leiomyosarcomas are malignant smooth muscle tumors, but the specific vascular nature of the tumor and its location are less characteristic of leiomyosarcoma, which does not typically present with the same degree of vascularity as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would not typically cause a vascular, extradural mass with skull destruction and the specific histological and immunohistochemical features seen in this case, making it an unlikely diagnosis.
